owner_direction: Resolve the measurement authorization mismatch first. R02–R03 require a current baseline before completing GPS-C01 but explicitly withhold benchmark and instrumentation authorization. Provide bounded permission for those measurements, using existing tooling first.

Finish the shared engineering contract. Define redraw ownership; what pointer, camera, and scroll changes invalidate; geometry/text/upload reuse; cache lifetime; and common scrolling, clipping, and hit-testing behavior. Preserve legitimate differences between terminal rows and continuous scrolling. Specify measurable correctness and performance expectations.

Implement and verify bounded Rust changes against that contract. Use the baseline to choose the first change. Window-local invalidation is a plausible candidate, not yet a measured priority. Keep all 25 regression obligations, but execute relevant proof with each implementation slice; reserve complete adoption and endurance qualification for final acceptance.

The existing plan already separates specification approval from implementation acceptance. We should honor that distinction: define the proof before implementation; do not demand completed production proof before allowing implementation.
Retain the engineering requirements and correct the sequencing—not discard the specification, replace the renderer wholesale, or add another approval framework.
bounded_implementation_direction: Choose by baseline and define engineering contract and slice proof first; preserve specification approval and final implementation acceptance distinction.

bounded_correction_scope.interpretation: The explicit request to implement and verify bounded Rust changes authorizes this baseline-selected correction to existing camera behavior after defining its contract and proof. It does not approve the proposed cross-cutting mechanisms, numeric budgets or final product acceptance.
